card.title: Speed and velocity
card.body: **Average speed** is distance divided by elapsed time, $v_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{d}{\Delta t}$ (scalar). **Average velocity** is displacement divided by elapsed time, $\vec{v}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{\Delta\vec{x}}{\Delta t}$ (vector in the direction of $\Delta\vec{x}$). At a single instant, the magnitude of instantaneous velocity equals instantaneous speed.
card.says: speed tells you how fast you cover ground; velocity tells you how fast and in which direction your position changes.
card.from: comparing how much distance or displacement happens in each second of elapsed time.
card.useWhen: the problem distinguishes direction, reversals, or signs along an axis — velocity carries a sign or direction, whereas speed does not.
card.example: Run $80\text{ m}$ east and then $20\text{ m}$ west in $20\text{ s}$. Distance $d = 80 + 20 = 100\text{ m}$, so average speed $v_{\text{av}} = 100 / 20 = 5\text{ m/s}$. Displacement $\Delta x = 80 - 20 = +60\text{ m}$ east, so average velocity is $60 / 20 = 3\text{ m/s}$ east.
card.analogy: Speed is the number on a car's speedometer; velocity is the speedometer together with the compass showing which way you are heading.

aliases: อัตราเร็วและความเร็ว
